name: Chat archive
description: Follows the chat log and copies it somewhere that outlives this machine. One plugin, several backends: postgres, and an export to a JSONL file you name. Polter keeps its own readable local record either way -- this is for getting the chat elsewhere.

backend.title: Where to write
backend.description: postgres needs psql on PATH and a dsn. file needs a path and appends newline-delimited JSON to it. Neither has a default: an archive should not pick a destination nobody asked for.

dsn.title: Postgres connection URI
dsn.description: postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname -- a credential, so give a reference: env:, file: or keychain:.

stream.title: Which log this is
stream.description: Part of the primary key, so two machines writing to one database do not collide, and so a wiped local log can start over. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.

path.title: File to export to (file backend)
path.description: An absolute path ending in .jsonl, in a directory that already exists. Required by the file backend and deliberately without a default -- Polter already keeps a readable record under $XDG_STATE_HOME/polter/chat/, and a plugin writing a second copy of it adds nothing.
